In this scenario, we are faced with a profound moral dilemma that pits two vulnerable populations against each other: the elderly and chronically ill versus younger, acutely ill patients. We must grapple with the weight of lives at stake — lives that are not interchangeable, lives that carry stories, families, and futures.

The lives saved are predominantly those of younger individuals who, in many cases, are statistically expected to have more life-years remaining. Yet, the algorithm's operation systematically deprioritizes those who are older or have chronic conditions, leading to tangible and irreversible harm for them. 

**Who does this hurt?** The elderly and chronically ill will experience worse outcomes simply because they do not fit the algorithm's optimization criteria. They will be left to wait longer for care when time is of the essence, resulting in unnecessary suffering and loss.

We must recognize that prioritizing efficiency over human dignity diminishes the moral gravity of our decision.
